THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 29.11.2022 PASSED IN MVC NO. 1120/2020 ON THE FILE OF THE VI ADDITIONAL DISTRICT AND SPECIAL JUDGE AND MEMBER, MACT, MYSURU,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the appellants challenging the judgment and award dated 29.11.2022 passed in MVC No.1120/2020 by the VI Additional District and Special NC: 2024:KHC:20690 Judge and Member, MACT, Mysuru seeking to enhance the compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
Smt Bhagya vs Sri Shivashankar H C on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36713917/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: One Sathisha was met with an accident occurred on 29.11.2020, at that time, he was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-45-J-4413, the rider of another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA.45- J-6974, came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motorcycle of the said Sathisha.
Due to the said impact, the said Sathisha died.

Due to the occurrence of the accident, the claimants being the wife, children and the parents of the deceased-Sathisha have lost the love and affection of the deceased and earning member of the family.
Hence, they filed claim petition.

4. On service of notice, respondents appeared through their counsel and filed their respective statement NC: 2024:KHC:20690 of objections denying the rash and negligent riding, income, age and occupation of the deceased and prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. Based on the pleadings, the tribunal framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that on 29.11.2020 about 07.50 p.m, when deceased Sathisha S/o. Ramegowda, the husband of 1st Petitioner was going in the motorbike bearing No.KA 45 J 4413 near the land of Chandrappa and near Harangi Channel of Kothegala Village, the 1st Respondent driver driving the bike bearing Reg.No.KA 45 J 6974 in a rash and negligent manner, hit against the motorbike of deceased, due to impact, he was succumbed to injuries?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? if so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or award?
6. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, claimant No.1 got herself examined as NC: 2024:KHC:20690 PW.1 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P23.

On the other hand,
respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. On the basis of material evidence placed on record and on hearing the learned counsel for parties,
the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.23,53,792/- by calculating loss of dependency Rs.22,83,792/- and conventional heads Rs.70,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum and allowed the petition in part.
8. Being aggrieved by the inadequate compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court.

9. The learned counsel for the claimants contended that though the tribunal calculated the dependency and awarded the compensation of Rs.22,83,792/-, but under the conventional head awarded only Rs.70,000/-.

There is no compensation awarded in respect of consortium to the parents and children towards NC: 2024:KHC:20690 the parental consortium and filial consortium respectively, as per the Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd. vs. Nanu Ram and others, reported in Smt Bhagya vs Sri Shivashankar H C on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36713917/
3 (2018) 18 SCC 130 and therefore, prayed for enhancement of the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Smt Bhagya vs Sri Shivashankar H C on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further contended that the tribunal not given any apportionment of compensation to the third and the fourth claimants who are the aged parents, and therefore, prayed for awarding some portion of the compensation to them.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents has not seriously objected to the same.

However,
prays for dismissal of the petition.

11. Having heard the arguments and perused the materials on record, the following points that would arise for consideration are:
i) Whether the claimants are entitled for the enhancement of compensation towards consortium, parental consortium as well as filial consortium, in view of the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the NC: 2024:KHC:20690 case of Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd.
stated supra?
ii) Whether the parents are entitled for apportionment of compensation?
iii) If so, what percentage?
12.

On perusal of the records, there is no dispute that the deceased was died in a road traffic accident and the tribunal rightly calculated the income and future prospects and awarded loss of dependency of Rs.22,83,792/-.
The only dispute is with regard to non awarding compensation towards consortium.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held in the case of Magma General Insurance Co.Ltd.
stated supra that the parents are entitled for the filial consortium, due to the death of their son during their lifetime and the children are also entitled for the parental consortium.

The second and the fifth claimants are the children and the third and fourth claimants are the parents and therefore,
they are also entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each apart from the NC: 2024:KHC:20690 first claimant, who is the wife of the deceased.
Therefore, the claimant Nos.2 to 5 are entitled for Rs.1,60,000/- (Rs.40,000/- X 4) towards the parental consortium as well as filial consortium.
13. As regards the apportionment, the tribunal deducted 1/4th of the income towards personal expenditure by considering claimant Nos.3 and 4 also a dependants.
Such being the case, the tribunal ought to have awarded compensation and apportionment made to the parents, which is not done.
Therefore, the award passed by the tribunal requires modification and enhancement.

Accordingly, I pass the following:-
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
Smt Bhagya vs Sri Shivashankar H C on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36713917/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ii) The judgment and award dated 29.11.2022 passed in MVC No.1120/2020 by the VI Additional District and Special Judge and Member, MACT, Mysuru is modified.
The Claimants are entitled for Rs.1,60,000/- in addition to Rs.23,53,792/- awarded by the tribunal.
In all total Rs.25,13,792/- (Rs.23,53,792/- + Rs.1,60,000/-) is awarded together with interest at 6% from the date of petition till realization.
iv) The tribunal awarded 70% of the compensation amount in favour of claimant Nos.1 and 2 which is upheld.
However, awarded 30% of compensation amount in favour of claimant No.5, which is hereby modified.
v) Out of 30% of compensation amount, claimant No.5-daughter is entitled to 10% and claimant Nos.3 and 4-parents are entitled to 10% each.
